title: Look at the implied volatility term structure before you pick an expiry
summary: Advanced traders look at implied volatility; the speaker says professionals look at the volatility term structure, implied volatility across expiries. You may need to dig on your broker's option page; his broker calls it IV index. If you are thinking about calendar spreads or diagonals, it is a good place to start because it helps you choose your expiration.

params.label: Near-expiry IV
params.help: One point on the term structure.

params.label: Far-expiry IV
params.help: A second point on the term structure. Change the gap to see the effect.

params.label: Chart range IV
params.help: Only sets the price range drawn.

steps.caption: Each expiry has its own implied volatility. Across expiries that is the term structure (his broker calls it IV index).
Illustration: a calendar at $100, selling the 30-day call (IV 32%) and buying the 90-day call (IV 27%).
The calendar's vega depends on both expiries, so the IV of each expiry on the term structure matters.
Theta as the near expiry approaches: the near and far legs decay at different rates.
Speaker's point: for calendars and diagonals, start with the term structure to choose your expirations.

takeaways: Advanced traders look at implied volatility; professionals look at its term structure across expiries.
You may have to dig for it on your broker's option page; his broker calls it IV index.
For calendar spreads or diagonals, the term structure is a good place to start because it helps you choose the expiration.
caveats: The transcript is cut mid-sentence and does not say which expiries to buy or sell.
The calendar, strikes and IV levels are added illustration, not from the clip.
